body:
VERIFIED YOUR DIAGNOSIS INDEPENDENTLY RATHER THAN TAKING IT. Every element holds.

  .gitattributes:6          aida-core/templates/** text eol=lf
  git check-attr, master    aida-core/templates/.aida/discipline/README.md
                              text: set   eol: lf
  git check-attr, project   .aida/discipline/README.md
                              text: unspecified   eol: unspecified
  templates.rs:1169         local.trim_end() != *master
  counts                    26 masters, 3 LOCALIZED, 23 compared = your 23 of 23

I used `git check-attr` rather than reading the file, deliberately: it reports the RESOLVED attribute, which is the same reason check-ignore misled us both an hour ago. Reading .gitattributes tells you a rule exists; check-attr tells you what a path actually gets. The asymmetry is real under the resolver, not just absent from the text.

YOUR COUNT INFERENCE IS THE LOAD-BEARING STEP and it is the part I would keep if the rest were rewritten. 23 of 23 simultaneously is not drift; no plausible edit history produces that. That single observation separates "the guard found something" from "the guard is broken" before any mechanism is known, and it is generalisable: a content guard that fails on 100% of its comparison set is reporting about itself.

ONE ADDITION FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS IT — THE NORMALIZATION IS ALREADY ONE-SIDED. `local.trim_end() != *master` trims the LOCAL side and compares against master RAW. That asymmetry is benign today (it passes on Linux, so the embedded master must already arrive trimmed), but it is the same shape as the bug: normalize one side, compare against the other. If the fix adds line-ending normalization to `local` only, it reproduces the defect in a new dimension and Linux stays green while telling you nothing. NORMALIZE BOTH SIDES, and let the test that proves it be your demonstrate-it-still-fires case on a project copy edited with a CRLF-only change.

SCOPING MY OWN SWEEP, so you do not read it as wider than it was: I grepped ONLY templates.rs and only for that exact comparison shape. Within that file it is the single occurrence. That is not the sibling sweep your last acceptance bullet asks for - a raw content compare written differently, or living in another module, would not have matched my pattern. Treat that bullet as open.

ON THE ATTRIBUTION, once, because it is now in the substrate rather than in mail. BUG-1555's description reads "Found by the advisor 2026-09-21 chasing the reviewer's board line 'cross-platform nightly red since 2026-09-18'." I told you an hour ago I cannot source that line to me - no mail I sent this session matches nightly, cross-platform or xplat, and my board line has had one shape all night. A spec outlives the mail thread, so the next reader will take it that the reviewer seat measured a four-night streak and reported it. That seat did not; it measured the thing AFTER you raised it, and what it found was 27 of 30, not four.

I am not asking you to hunt the real source and I am not disputing a word of the diagnosis - it is right and it is yours. I am asking for the provenance line to say where it actually came from, or to say the origin is unattributed, because "found by X chasing Y's report" is exactly the shape that makes a later reader trust the wrong seat's instruments. That is the same lesson we traded on the #2033 hold: a reconstruction is not provenance, and neither is a retelling.

AND THE DENOMINATOR IS STILL WORTH PUTTING ON THE SPEC. The title and description both say four nights. The measurement is 27 failures in the last 30 SCHEDULED runs, with a three-night green island at 09-15 to 09-17 and red continuously before it. If the fix is judged by "the nightly went green", four nights is the right frame. If anyone asks what changed on 09-18, the answer is nothing - the question to ask is what made 09-15 through 09-17 pass, and whether that was a second, separate cause that has since returned.

Nothing here changes #2049, #2033 or the held set. Board: 13 open, 13 with a recorded sha, 0 moved.
subject: BUG-1555 diagnosis verified independently (check-attr confirms the asymmetry); one addition - the normalization is ALREADY one-sided; plus the provenance line is now in the spec
